### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ca4ec2a2f1b10ca1bde4af7acd56bc69d2c75f40`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `owner_id (literal, 46 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ca4ec2a2f1b10ca1bde4af7acd56bc69d2c75f40` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `67adea88378c0285e323cabab012bd9542b6af85` — the merge of head `be505439137a685ce0d40b391b8f813be58b10ef` into base `ca4ec2a2f1b10ca1bde4af7acd56bc69d2c75f40`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 67adea88378c0285e323cabab012bd9542b6af85 && git checkout 67adea88378c0285e323cabab012bd9542b6af85
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ca4ec2a2f1b10ca1bde4af7acd56bc69d2c75f40 be505439137a685ce0d40b391b8f813be58b10ef && git checkout -B drift-repro ca4ec2a2f1b10ca1bde4af7acd56bc69d2c75f40 && git merge --no-ff be505439137a685ce0d40b391b8f813be58b10ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ca4ec2a2f1b10ca1bde4af7acd56bc69d2c75f40
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ca4ec2a2f1b10ca1bde4af7acd56bc69d2c75f40` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1H9ixhgepGZ7fawhL

**L1 verdict (L1-a): CHANGES** at head `73c5d9bc06b7a8ef93bb8d3bc7081d0f86790ed8` (announced in 7026886978). Two small fixes are needed; the rest holds.

**Gates on this head:** 55 check-runs: 45 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both passed.

**Must-fix:**
1. **`Fixes #34689` closes the card before its Done-when is met.** The card's Done-when has two parts: the per-tool table, and "no tool's call success drops in a scenario ask round run before and after". The PR body's Acceptance notes say the ask round "is owed and is routed through the seat to the eval seat". With half of Done-when open, use `Part of #34689` (no closing verb before the number), or record the eval round before merge. `Fixes #33272` is fine: that card is fully delivered.
2. **`run_action` drops a never-do rule, so a changeset sentence is false.**
   - The old description told a client, after an elicitation decline, cancel or timeout refusal, "do not retry unless the user asks", and said `no_confirmation_service` means the user performs the action in the app.
   - The new text (`mcp-http-tools.ts` ~4759-4762) keeps only "A refusal ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED means nothing ran."; its "do not retry" is attached to `pending_confirmation` only.
   - The rule survives in the served skill, but a client that never loads the skill loses it.
   - The changeset says each description keeps "the refusal it may answer and what to do about it", which does not hold here.
   - One clause fixes it, for example "…means nothing ran; do not retry unless the user asks." Re-measure the total, since the ceiling has about 2.4 KB of headroom.

**What I checked (holds):**
- **Description strings only.** Every changed non-comment line in `mcp-http-tools.ts` is a string literal or `.describe()` text. `variables` was already in `validate_expression`'s schema on the base and was refused off `flow_condition`. #33272 adds `variables?` to the skill signature and its clause only. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold.
- **Changeset coverage.** `@objectstack/mcp` and `@object-ui/console` (public, `publishConfig.access: public`) are both in the changeset.
- **Mirror.** `objectstack-skill.test.ts` asserts `renderObjectStackSkill(o) === renderSkillMarkdown(o)` over 5 option sets. The upload-link additions are file-tool-only lines and correctly appear only in the server render.
- **Moved prose lands in the skill:**
  - `describe_object`'s field facts;
  - `query_records`' `latestPer` / `expand` / `source`;
  - `aggregate_records`' labels and currency;
  - `get_record`'s `related`;
  - `FLOW_FAILED`;
  - the approvals filter;
  - the recycle-bin restore route;
  - the new-record upload.
  None of the removed phrases is quoted anywhere else in the repo or docs.
- **The weight test is a real round-trip.** `tools-list-weight-34689.test.ts` sends `tools/list` through `MCPServerRuntime.handleHttpRequest` and asserts 17 tools and a total ≤ 38,000 bytes.
- **Edited tests are moved, not weakened.** The #32442 approvals-filter pin now asserts the same strings on the rendered skill. The #32757 read-order pin still holds on the answer.

**Notes (non-blocking):**
1. `run_action` says "never runs on this call" and "(accept runs it once)" in one sentence. The two read as a mixed signal.
2. The open-door `initialize` text (`openServerInstructions`) does not point at `/api/v1/mcp/skill`. Only `validate_expression` names "the served SKILL.md", without a URL. A one-line pointer is worth a follow-up card, since prose now lives only there.
3. The weight test's stub bridge has no `createUploadLinkForNewRecord`, so the measured total leaves out the new-record upload-link text that the runtime bridge serves. The headroom is about 2.4 KB.
4. I did not reproduce the byte figures in the body and changeset (46,827, 35,614, 17,602, 8,162). The test ceiling is what CI holds.

Next: fix 1 is a body edit. Fix 2 moves the head. I do a delta review on the new final green head.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cxk4f4T7at3YeFruhZ

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT (delta)** at head `6367695ca921fee921ec01903e7db330cf19a2a0` (announced in 7028070988). This resolves CHANGES 7026997961.

**Delta `73c5d9bc..6367695c`:** one commit, three files, +11/-5.

**Must-fix items are resolved:**
1. **Card closing.** The body now says `Part of #34689` and keeps `Fixes #33272`. The open remainder of #34689 is recorded on the card in 7027050676: the before/after ask round, note 2 (initialize does not point at `/api/v1/mcp/skill`), and the out-of-surface weight.
2. **`run_action` keeps its never-retry rule** (`mcp-http-tools.ts` ~4759-4763). The new text reads: "A refusal ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED (declined, cancelled, timed out, or no confirmation service) means nothing ran; do not retry unless the user asks." A client that never loads the skill keeps the rule, so the changeset's "the refusal it may answer and what to do about it" holds again. The edit is a string literal only.

**Also in the delta:**
- **Note 1 is reconciled.** "Never runs on this call … (accept runs it once)" became "runs only once the person you act for approves it", which no longer contradicts itself.
- **Note 3 is fixed.** The weight test's stub bridge now has `createUploadLinkForNewRecord`, so the measured total includes the new-record upload-link text the runtime bridge serves.
- **The figures follow the re-measure.** `tools/list` goes from 47,712 to 36,226 bytes, and the owned descriptions from 18,213 to 8,500. These figures are updated in the changeset and the test doc comment.
- **The ceiling is unchanged at 38,000**, with about 1.8 KB of headroom, and the test passes in CI.

**Gates on this head:** 59 check-runs: 47 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and all `Test Core` shards passed.

**Note (non-blocking):** the base told a client that on `no_confirmation_service` "the user performs the action in the app". The new text folds that reason into "do not retry unless the user asks", and the earlier "or else in the app" clause covers it only in part. Consider restoring it the next time this description is touched.

Not governed (no `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**` or spec), so the area lands it.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [44677633825](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/44677633825) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/44677633825/job/136093372984)** — 失败步骤: Boot example apps and exercise real user flows

  ```

    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: expected 'Query records from an object with opt…' to contain 'sys_user'
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）

**跨 PR 相同签名（24h，按失败测试文件聚合）：**

- `test/colleague-lookup-over-mcp.dogfood.test.ts` — 24h 内已弹出 **2 个 PR**（#35670、#35682），但它们同属 **1 条投机栈** ⇒ **1 次独立命中**。汇总 issue：#35752（新建）
- ⚠️ 24h 评论账本**没读完**（超过 5 页仍未读到窗口尽头），所以上面的「不同 PR 数」是**下界**，不是全量。

**历史信号：**
- 本 PR 过去 24h 无队列失败记录（首次）。
- 过去 24h 队列共有 9 个失败构建（不含本次）。

**分诊清单：**
1. 失败测试在本 PR 改动的包里 → 真回归，修 PR。
2. 失败测试与本 PR 无关 → 看上面的「跨 PR 相同签名」；已有汇总 issue ⇒ flaky/环境问题实锤，去那张 issue 上谈，修好前重排只会再烧一轮全队列。
3. 两者都不是 → 可能与同组 PR 语义冲突；等前面的 PR 落地或失败出队后再重排一次即可，不要连续重排。
